original_question: Does every zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space admit a left-topological group structure? Equivalently, if a compact space is zero-dimensional and homogeneous, must there exist a group operation on its underlying set together with a topology invariant under all left shifts x ↦ g x? In particular, if K is a first-countable zero-dimensional compact space, does its countable power K^ω admit the structure of a left-topological group?
target_in_paper: Problem 7 (Protasov): "Does every zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space admit the structure of a left topological group? In particular, does the countable power K^ω of a first-countable zero-dimensional compact space K admit the structure of a left topological group?"
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right problem and preserves both parts of the paper’s formulation: the general question about zero-dimensional compact homogeneous spaces and the special case of K^ω for first-countable zero-dimensional compact K. It also correctly unpacks the relevant notion of a left-topological group in terms of invariance under left shifts.
missing_details: The paper asks whether the given topology of the space can serve as the topology of a left-topological group; your paraphrase could be read as allowing a new topology on the same underlying set.
For paper-faithfulness, "zero-dimensional" should follow the paper’s notation: dim X = 0.
"Homogeneous" should be stated explicitly as topological homogeneity: for any x,y in X there exists a homeomorphism h:X->X with h(x)=y.
In the special case, K^ω is the countable product of K with the product topology.

The K^ω clause is only a particular instance of the main question, not an equivalent reformulation; the paper justifies it by citing Motorov’s theorem that K^ω is homogeneous when K is first-countable, zero-dimensional, and compact.

The arXiv version appends footnote 1 noting that this problem was later answered negatively by Banakh (Mat. Stud. 29 (2008), 215–217), so the paper no longer presents it as open without qualification.
refined_question: Let X be a zero-dimensional compact homogeneous topological space, where zero-dimensional means dim X = 0. Must there exist a group operation on the underlying set X such that, with its given compact topology τ, the pair (X,τ) is a left-topological group, i.e. τ is invariant under every left shift l_g:x -> gx? In particular, if K is a first-countable zero-dimensional compact space, does the product space K^ω admit such a left-topological group structure?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: it is stated verbatim as Problem 7, immediately after the paper defines what it means by a left-topological group, and the paper’s only nearby sharpening is the "in particular" K^ω case, justified by Motorov’s theorem. I did not give a separate alternate formulation because the K^ω clause is presented only as a special case, not as an equivalence. The main tightening needed was to make explicit that the existing compact/product topology is the one to be used for the left-topological group structure, and to record the paper’s notation that zero-dimensional means dim X = 0.
